title: Deny whole-tree git verbs while more than one worker is live
action: P1 FRICTION, independently confirmed by the review session's security reviewer: `checkGitBashCommand` (packages/bee/lib/guards.mjs ~:451) returns null unless the phase is in TERMINAL_PHASES (~:151), so during `swarming` NOTHING mechanically stops a subagent running `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, `git checkout .` or `git clean -fd` in a shared checkout. This is not theoretical: in one parallel wave today it happened three times — two index sweeps that destroyed commit attribution, and one whole-tree revert that DELETED a live worker's in-progress edit while that worker held a valid file reservation (reservations govern files; the tree is not a file). The rules shipped as prose only. FIX: extend checkGitBashCommand so that when the runtime has MORE THAN ONE live worker (the computed live view, not the stored array — see how active workers are derived elsewhere in the lib), a whole-tree git verb is REFUSED with a typed message naming the verb, why it is unsafe with concurrent workers, and the sanctioned alternatives: status / diff / log, and a single path-scoped commit made through the worker's own temp index (GIT_INDEX_FILE + read-tree/update-index/write-tree/commit-tree/update-ref), with `git add -N` on new paths as the fallback. Scope the denial precisely — a single-worker session and the orchestrator's own release/merge work must stay unaffected, and a genuinely path-scoped `git commit -- <paths>` must remain allowed. Fail-open on any resolution error the way the surrounding guard code already does, EXCEPT that an unresolvable worker count is treated as multi-worker (the conservative side, matching the debt guards' 'unreadable means debt' discipline). Add tests in the owning suite for: refusal of each whole-tree verb under multi-worker, allowance under single-worker, allowance of path-scoped commit and of status/diff/log, and the unresolvable-count case refusing. You MAY run the guard suite(s) that own checkGitBashCommand (locate them; likely skills/bee-hive/templates/tests/test_guards.mjs and/or packages/bee/tests) and must quote them. GIT SAFETY: obey the very rule you are implementing — temp-index commit only.

truths: A whole-tree git verb is refused with a typed message while more than one worker is live; the message names the sanctioned alternatives.
Single-worker sessions, path-scoped commits, and status/diff/log are unaffected.
An unresolvable worker count refuses (conservative), other resolution errors fail open as the surrounding code does.
Tests cover each case and are green (quote the suite lines).
prohibitions: Do NOT block the orchestrator's own release/merge git work.
Do NOT touch packages/bee/bee.mjs or lib/state.mjs (sibling cell owns them).

regen_obligation_ack: wave-barrier: regen owned by MAIN at feature close (parallel-default D2)

trace.outcome: Whole-tree git verbs (reset/stash/clean/checkout/restore/revert/rebase/merge/cherry-pick/apply, plus git add and un-path-scoped git commit) now refuse with a typed git-concurrent-tree verdict whenever the computed live-worker view shows >1 worker in this checkout — phase-independent (swarming included) and with no config opt-out. The count unions active reservation agents with claims.mjs activeWorkers, de-duped by session and scoped to the acting workspace_id; an unresolvable count refuses (conservative), every other resolution error keeps the file's fail-open posture. Solo sessions, the orchestrator's release/merge work, read-only git, path-scoped 'git commit -- <paths>', 'git add -N', 'git stash list/show', 'git apply --check', and the full temp-index route stay allowed. Owning suite green: node packages/bee/tests/test_guards.mjs -> 58 passed, 0 failed, including 8 new gc-2 rows.
deviations: 1. Cell file paths were stale. `skills/bee-hive/templates/lib/guards.mjs` and
`skills/bee-hive/templates/tests/test_guards.mjs` do not exist — the guard lib
and its owning suite live at `packages/bee/lib/guards.mjs` and
`packages/bee/tests/test_guards.mjs`. Implemented and tested there. The cell's
`verify` command (`node skills/bee-hive/templates/tests/test_guards.mjs`) is
therefore not runnable as written; MAIN should run
`node packages/bee/tests/test_guards.mjs`.
2. Auto-fixed a stale comment in `packages/bee/hooks/bee-write-guard.mjs` (~:1222)
that asserted `checkGitBashCommand` "returns null unless the phase is terminal
— everywhere else this is a no-op". That is now false, and a comment declaring a
safety guard inert is exactly what invites a future editor to drop the call.
Comment text only, no behavior change; path was reserved before editing.
3. Scope call — `git rm` / `git mv` are deliberately NOT denied. They are
path-scoped by nature and were not part of the incident class; denying them
would be over-block with no evidence behind it. Documented in the code.
4. Scope call — `git add` is denied under multi-worker (not only the whole-tree
forms), because it stages into the SHARED index, which is the mechanism of the
two attribution-loss incidents. `git add -N` / `--intent-to-add` stays allowed
as the cell's named fallback.
5. Design finding worth carrying forward: `activeWorkers` alone would NOT have
caught today's incident. Worker subagents inside one Claude session share one
session id and one heartbeat, so the derived live-session view reports a
three-worker wave as ONE worker. The count therefore unions active reservation
agents (`session::agent`) with derived live sessions, de-duplicated by session,
and scoped to the acting workspace so a worker in another worktree never
over-blocks this checkout.
